'''Solra''', also known as the '''Elder Tongue''', is the ceremonial and liturgical language of [[Solara]]. It is the older prestige language from which the modern [[Solaran Language]] developed.

In Solaran tradition, Solra is associated with temples, state ritual, legal formulae, astronomy, ritual calendars, archives, and the most formal diplomatic language. It is not the ordinary language of the modern Solaran public.

The extracted source links Solra to [[Sonism]], but the exact relationship between the religion, temple institutions, and the Elder Tongue is still open.

== Historical Role ==

Source material places Solra's codification in an early dynastic or temple-centered period. Sun-temples and scribal colleges used the language to preserve ritual calendars, astronomical records, legal canons, hymns, and ceremonial formulae.

As ordinary speech changed over time, Solra remained deliberately conservative. This made it difficult to master but useful as a marker of continuity, authority, and elite education.

== Script And Learning ==

The source describes Solra as written in a right-to-left abugida with a complex vowel and diacritic system. Because the extracted glyph table is corrupted, this draft keeps only the high-level point: Solra used a difficult classical script distinct from the modern [[Solaran Alphabet|Sunline]] alphabet.

Training in Solra was traditionally associated with clergy, archivists, legal specialists, scholarly orders, and high state service. [[Elder Tongue Scribal Institutions]] maintained standards for the language and trained specialist readers, calligraphers, and teachers.

== Relationship To The State ==

Solara's modern state is a parliamentary democracy, but the source uses ceremonial language such as "Sun Throne" and "royal bureaucracy." This draft treats those terms cautiously as historical, ritual, or inherited ceremonial vocabulary until the constitutional role of older Solaran monarchy is confirmed.

Solra remained useful for formal proclamations and ceremonial legitimacy, but public comprehension required [[Solaran Language|Solaran]] translations in the [[Solaran Alphabet|Sunline]] alphabet.

== Modern Position By 1994 ==

By 1994, Solra was a protected prestige language rather than a mass vernacular. Its survival helped Solara present itself as both modern and ancient: a literate parliamentary nation with a strong ceremonial memory.

The language's difficulty also limited access. That made it an elite cultural asset, but it prevented Solra from replacing Solaran in mass education, newspapers, military communication, or ordinary administration.

== Canon Notes ==

The source gives later named institutional references from 2007-2009 and a modern literacy estimate. This 1994-back draft does not use those as fixed 1994 facts.

The source's "Sun Throne" and "royal bureaucracy" language needs later review against Solara's established parliamentary-democratic canon.
